en: to burn; to ignite; to set on fire

examples.en: You must not burn trash carelessly.
He practiced all night, burning with passion.
I burned the old letters in the yard.
The smell of burning fallen leaves feels like autumn.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 마지막 경기에 모든 힘을 불태워요.
examples.en: That player puts everything into the final game.

examples.ko: 지난 일을 잊으려고 사진들을 불태우고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to burn the photos to forget the past.

explain: '태우다'보다 활활 다 태워 없애는 느낌이 강해요. 불 자체뿐 아니라 열정, 투지 같은 마음에도 비유로 써요. 저절로 타는 건 '불타다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: He poured all his passion into the stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 온 힘과 마음을 다한다는 뜻의 비유예요. 운동, 공연, 공부처럼 노력하는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to say someone gives all their energy and heart to something. It is used for effort in sports, performances, studying, and so on.

explain_en: Someone deliberately ignites something, or pours passion into it. It has a stronger sense of burning something up completely than '태우다'. It is used not only for real fire but also figuratively for feelings like passion and fighting spirit. When something burns on its own, use '불타다'.

t90.ax: You must not burn trash carelessly.

examples.en: I cut my long hair off with a snip at the hair salon.
Please snip the string with scissors.
Mom cut up the vegetables with quick chops.
The gardener snipped off the tree branches.
I cut my bangs off too short and I regret it.
I snipped out the paper and made a card.

explain: 가위나 칼로 단번에 베어 자르는 소리나 모양이에요. 한 번 자르면 '싹둑', 여러 번 자르면 '싹둑싹둑'이라고 해요. 같은 느낌인데 더 크고 굵은 것은 '썩둑'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Mom chopped the vegetables snip by snip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 번 자를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cutting several times.

phrases.en: I cut the big radish with a chop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '싹둑'보다 크고 굵은 것을 자르는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like cutting something bigger and thicker.

phrases.en: I snipped out the colored paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이나 천을 가위로 오려 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for cutting paper or cloth out with scissors.

explain_en: It imitates the sound or look of cutting something in one stroke with scissors or a knife. One cut is '싹둑' and repeated cuts are '싹둑싹둑'. A bigger, thicker version of the same feel is '썩둑'.

examples.ko: 이 정수기는 여과 장치가 세 단계예요.
examples.en: This water purifier has a three-stage filtration system.
After filtration, the water becomes much cleaner.

examples.ko: 여과 필터는 석 달마다 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: You have to replace the filter every three months.

examples.ko: 그는 생각을 여과 없이 말해서 가끔 오해를 받아요.
examples.en: He says what he thinks without any filter, so he is sometimes misunderstood.

examples.ko: 여과가 잘 안 되면 물이 탁해요.
examples.en: If the filtering doesn't work well, the water looks cloudy.

examples.ko: 커피는 여과 방식에 따라 맛이 달라요.
examples.en: Coffee tastes different depending on the filtering method.

explain: 물이나 공기를 거르는 일이지만, 말과 정보를 걸러 낼 때도 비유로 써요. 일상에서는 '거르다'라고 하고, '여과 없이'는 생각이나 말을 그대로 드러낼 때 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그의 발언이 여과 없이 방송에 나갔어요.
phrases.en: His remarks were aired without any editing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 영상을 다듬거나 걸러 내지 않고 그대로 드러낼 때 써요. 좋게도 나쁘게도 쓰지만 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when words or footage are shown as they are, without being polished or screened. It can be positive or negative and often appears in news and writing.

explain_en: It refers to filtering water or air, but it is also used figuratively for filtering words and information. In everyday speech people say '거르다', and '여과 없이' is common for showing thoughts or words just as they are.

en: to lower; to worsen; to impair

examples.en: Noise lowers work performance.
They say stress weakens immunity.
A bad posture reduced my concentration.
We are looking for what lowers the quality.

examples.ko: 약이 판단력을 저하시킬 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: The medicine can impair judgment, so be careful.
Unnecessary features slowed it down, so I deleted them.

explain: 저하시키다는 어떤 원인이 수준이나 능력을 낮출 때 써요. 주어에는 사람보다 '소음, 스트레스, 피로, 나쁜 습관' 같은 원인이 많이 와요. 같은 뜻으로 '떨어뜨리다'는 말하기에 더 편해요.

phrases.en: Tiredness lowers your work speed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저하시키다'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 편하게 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 저하시키다 and more comfortable in everyday speech.

phrases.en: Bad posture lowers your study efficiency.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력, 효율, 품질 같은 말과 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A good collocation with words like ability, efficiency and quality.

phrases.example: 이 방법은 음식의 맛을 저하시키지 않아요.
phrases.en: This method does not make the food taste worse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 나빠지지 않는다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying that something does not make things worse.

explain_en: Formal, written — causing ability, quality or function to decline. 저하시키다 is used when some cause lowers a level or ability. The subject is more often a cause such as noise, stress, fatigue or a bad habit than a person. 떨어뜨리다 means much the same and is easier to say in speech.

examples.en: The teacher steered the topic in another direction.

examples.ko: 회사는 종이 문서를 전자 문서로 전환시켜요.
examples.en: The company converts paper documents into electronic ones.
I opened the window to change the mood.
They built a device that converts heat into electricity.
If you switch your way of thinking, the problem gets easy to solve.
They plan to shift the market toward online.

explain: '전환하다'와 거의 같아서 보통은 '전환하다'를 더 많이 써요. '전환시키다'는 누군가가 일부러 방향을 돌린다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 화제, 분위기, 방식 같은 말과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: The company changed its method.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전환시키다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form, used more often than 전환시키다.

phrases.en: He sang a song and changed the mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 분위기를 바꾸려는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests a deliberate effort to change the mood.

phrases.en: I changed the topic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word for everyday talk.

explain_en: Causative; someone makes something switch, like a channel or topic. It is almost the same as '전환하다', which people use more often. '전환시키다' has a stronger sense that someone deliberately turns things around. It goes with words like '화제', '분위기', '방식'.

t90.ax: I opened the window to change the mood.

en: to maintain; to sustain; to prolong

examples.en: This exercise keeps the effect going for a long time.

examples.ko: 좋은 습관을 지속시키려면 매일 조금씩 하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To keep a good habit going, it is best to do a little every day.

examples.ko: 회사는 이 서비스를 앞으로도 지속시킬 계획이에요.
examples.en: The company plans to keep this service running in the future too.

examples.ko: 그는 어려운 상황에서도 좋은 성적을 지속시켰어요.
examples.en: He kept his good grades going even in a hard situation.
Keeping people's interest going is the hardest part.
I am sorry I could not keep that enthusiasm going.

explain: '계속하다'는 하던 일을 이어서 하는 것이고, '지속시키다'는 상태나 효과가 끊기지 않게 하는 쪽이에요. 목적어로 '효과, 관계, 관심, 서비스'처럼 상태를 나타내는 말이 와요. 말할 때는 '유지하다'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I want to maintain a good relationship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '지속시키다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in speech than 지속시키다.

phrases.example: 이 방법으로 효과를 더 오래 지속시킬 수 있어요.
phrases.en: With this method, you can make the effect last longer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끊기지 않게 할 수 있다는 가능을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says it is possible to keep something from breaking off.

phrases.en: They kept their relationship going for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관계'처럼 상태를 나타내는 말과 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A good collocation, since 관계 is a state that can be kept going.

explain_en: You make a process or habit go on over time (습관을 지속시키다) '계속하다' means to carry on doing something, while '지속시키다' is about making a state or effect not break off. Its objects are state-like nouns such as '효과', '관계', '관심', '서비스'. In speech, '유지하다' is more common.

dis.h: make an action or process continue over time
gh: keep a state or condition as it is

p.n: 유지하다 sounds like keeping the effort at the same level rather than continuing it over time.

t90.ax: I am sorry I could not keep that enthusiasm going.

en: to spin; to turn; to rotate

examples.en: The machine spins its blades quickly.
Try rotating the picture to the right.
I rotated the phone photo by 90 degrees.
When you turn the wheel, the bicycle moves forward.
I turned the chair around and looked toward the window.
Where is the button that rotates the screen?

explain: 무언가를 빙글 돌게 만들 때 써요. 사진이나 화면을 돌리는 컴퓨터 말로도 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '돌리다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 스스로 도는 것은 '회전하다'예요.

phrases.en: Please turn the photo to the right.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회전시키다'의 일상적인 말이라서 대화에서는 이쪽이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word for '회전시키다', and more natural in conversation.

phrases.en: Turn the handle clockwise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명서에서 돌리는 방향을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in manuals to state which way to turn something.

phrases.en: Rotate the screen 90 degrees and look at it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도' 앞에 각도를 넣어 돌리는 정도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an angle before '도' to say how far to turn.

explain_en: Transitive — you make something rotate (화면을 회전시키다) It is used for making something spin around, and also as a computer term for rotating a photo or screen. In daily speech 돌리다 sounds far more natural. Something turning on its own is 회전하다.

t90.ax: The machine spins its blades quickly.

examples.en: I train my puppy every day.
The coach trained the players hard.
I've been put in charge of training the new hires.
I'm training my child to sleep alone.
Training a horse takes a long time.
We trained the staff and sent them out to the site.

explain: '~을 훈련시키다'는 내가 직접 하지 않고 대상이 훈련하게 만드는 말이에요. 내가 몸으로 연습하면 '훈련하다'예요. 같은 뜻으로 '훈련을 시키다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I train my puppy every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '훈련시키다'를 띄어 쓴 형태로 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of the same verb, with the same meaning.

phrases.en: I'm training the new employees these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 훈련을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for training that is going on right now.

phrases.en: Please train our dog well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 훈련을 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone else to do the training.

explain_en: Causative; make a person or animal practice. ~을 훈련시키다 means you make someone or something else go through training instead of doing it yourself. If you practice yourself, it is 훈련하다. You can also split it as 훈련을 시키다 with the same meaning.

dis.h: make someone or an animal practice
gh: cultivate skill or discipline, martial arts

p.n: 조련 is specifically animal taming/training; 훈련시키다 is general.

t90.ax: I train my puppy every day.

examples.en: When sperm and an egg cell meet, fertilization happens.

examples.ko: 여성은 한 달에 한 번 난자를 배출해요.
examples.en: A woman releases an egg cell once a month.

examples.ko: 난자 냉동 보관에 관한 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article about freezing egg cells.
I heard an explanation about egg donation.

examples.ko: 생물 시간에 난자와 정자의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In biology class, I learned the difference between eggs and sperm.
A fertilized egg grows into an embryo.

explain: 생물이나 의학에서 암컷의 생식세포를 말하고, 짝이 되는 말은 '정자'예요. 음식으로 먹는 달걀과는 다르고, 소리가 같은 다른 말이 있으니 문맥으로 구분해야 해요. 일상에서는 주로 수업, 뉴스, 병원 이야기에서 나와요.

phrases.en: A baby forms when a sperm and an egg meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말과 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, used together with its paired word.

phrases.en: I saw a news report about egg donation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in hospitals and the news.

phrases.en: Once the egg is fertilized, the cells start to divide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생물 수업이나 의학 이야기에서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression used in biology classes and medical talk.

explain_en: Biological egg cell of humans and animals; science context. It is the female reproductive cell in biology and medicine, and its pair is '정자' (sperm). It is not the egg you eat, which is '달걀'. Another word sounds the same, so tell them apart by context. In daily life it mostly comes up in classes, news and hospital talk.

t90.ax: A fertilized egg grows into an embryo.

examples.en: The baby has started to be toilet trained.

examples.ko: 아이 옷에 똥오줌이 묻어서 급히 빨았어요.
examples.en: The child's clothes got soiled, so I washed them quickly.
I heard that in the old days people used human waste as fertilizer.

examples.ko: 병원에서 환자의 똥오줌을 치우는 일을 도왔어요.
examples.en: At the hospital I helped clean up patients' waste.
I'm training the puppy to go in the right place.

examples.ko: 외양간 근처는 똥오줌 냄새가 심해서 못 가겠어요.
examples.en: The smell near the barn is so bad I can't go there.

explain: 똥과 오줌을 같이 부르는 구어예요. 병원이나 격식 있는 글에서는 '대소변'이라고 하고, 아이를 키울 때는 '똥오줌을 가리다'를 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 똥오줌 못 가리고 덤비지 말고 상황부터 파악해요.
phrases.en: Don't rush in without knowing what's what; first understand the situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분별력이 없거나 철없이 구는 사람을 나무랄 때 쓰는 속된 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A crude way to scold someone who has no judgment or acts without thinking.
phrases.en_equiv: not know one's head from one's elbow

explain_en: Plain native word; informal, used for babies, pets, and everyday talk. It is a colloquial word for feces and urine together. Hospitals and formal writing use '대소변', and in parenting people often say '똥오줌을 가리다' (to be toilet trained).

t90.ax: The baby has started to be toilet trained.

en: newborn's first jacket; traditional baby jacket

examples.en: I bought a newborn's jacket before the baby was born.

examples.ko: 엄마가 제 배냇저고리를 아직 보관하고 있어요.
examples.en: My mom still keeps my baby jacket.

examples.ko: 병원에서 갓 태어난 아기에게 배냇저고리를 입혀 줬어요.
examples.en: At the hospital they dressed the newborn baby in a baenaet-jeogori (first jacket).

examples.ko: 배냇저고리는 보통 흰색이나 연한 색이 많아요.
examples.en: Baenaet jackets are usually white or light colors.
My friend gave me a pretty baby jacket as a gift.
The newborn jacket was so tiny that it amazed me.

explain: 갓 태어난 아기에게 처음 입히는 작은 저고리예요. 아기 옷 전체를 말하는 게 아니라 이 옷만 가리켜요. 출산 준비물이나 육아 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The mother dressed the baby in a newborn jacket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입는 사람이 아기이니까 '입다'가 아니라 '입히다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since the baby is the one wearing it, use 입히다 rather than 입다.
phrases.en_equiv: to dress in a newborn jacket

phrases.en: Grandmother keeps Dad's newborn jacket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기념으로 오래 간직하는 물건이라 이 말과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It's often kept as a keepsake, so this pairing is natural.

phrases.en: I gave my friend a newborn jacket as a baby gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출산 선물로 흔히 주는 물건이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common baby gift.

explain_en: It is the small jacket put on a baby right after birth. It refers only to this garment, not to baby clothes in general. It often comes up when talking about birth preparations or child care.

examples.en: Cold makes metal contract.
When you contract your muscles, you use strength.
They say cold water constricts blood vessels.

examples.ko: 냉각 장치가 부품을 수축시켜서 꼭 맞게 만들었어요.
examples.en: The cooling device shrank the part so it fits tightly.
I heard the medicine has the effect of constricting blood vessels.

examples.ko: 운동 전에 근육을 수축시켰다 풀어 주세요.
examples.en: Before exercising, contract your muscles and then release them.

explain: 수축시키다는 어떤 힘이나 조건이 다른 것을 줄어들게 한다고 말할 때 써서 과학이나 건강 이야기에 주로 나와요. 스스로 줄어드는 것은 '수축하다/수축되다', 반대는 '팽창시키다'예요. 옷이 물에 줄어드는 일상 상황에서는 '줄다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Blood vessels contract when they touch cold water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 줄어드는 것은 '수축하다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '수축하다' for something shrinking by itself.

phrases.en: Heat makes metal expand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말로, 커지게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite, meaning to cause something to expand.

phrases.en: Hot water makes the fabric shrink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '수축시키다'를 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain everyday way to say '수축시키다'.

explain_en: Transitive — something causes another thing to contract (피부를 수축시키다) 수축시키다 says that some force or condition makes something shrink, so it appears mostly in science and health talk. Shrinking by itself is 수축하다 or 수축되다, and the opposite is 팽창시키다. For clothes that shrink in water, everyday Korean uses 줄다.

examples.ko: 신체장애가 있어도 일할 수 있는 직장이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Workplaces where people with physical disabilities can work are increasing.

examples.ko: 이 건물에는 신체장애 학생을 위한 엘리베이터가 있어요.
examples.en: This building has an elevator for students with physical disabilities.

examples.ko: 사고로 신체장애를 얻은 분이 강연을 하셨어요.
examples.en: A person who acquired a physical disability in an accident gave a talk.
Support differs depending on the degree of disability.

examples.ko: 신체장애 때문에 불편한 점을 이야기해 주셨어요.
examples.en: They told us about the inconveniences caused by their physical disability.

examples.ko: 신체장애 여부는 서류에 적지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: You don't have to write whether you have a physical disability on the form.

explain: 서류와 제도, 뉴스에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '장애'라고 하고, 사람을 가리킬 때는 '장애인'이라고 해요. 눈이 불편한 것은 '시각장애', 팔다리는 '지체장애'처럼 나눠서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 신체장애가 있는 사람도 편하게 탈 수 있는 버스예요.
phrases.en: It is a bus that people with physical disabilities can ride comfortably.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장애가 있는 상태를 설명할 때 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic expression for describing someone who has a physical disability.

phrases.example: 신체장애인 주차 구역에는 차를 세우면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not park in the parking area for people with physical disabilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 가리킬 때 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 그냥 '장애인'이라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person; in daily speech people often just say '장애인'.

phrases.example: 신체장애 등급에 따라 받는 지원이 달라요.
phrases.en: The support you receive differs depending on the disability grade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류와 제도에서 장애의 정도를 나눌 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal term used in documents and systems to classify the degree of disability.

explain_en: It is a formal term used in paperwork, systems and news. In daily life people simply say '장애', and for a person '장애인'. It can be narrowed down as '시각장애' (visual) or '지체장애' (limbs).

examples.ko: 요가를 하면 근육 이완에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Yoga helps relax your muscles.

examples.ko: 긴장을 풀고 몸의 이완을 느껴 보세요.
examples.en: Let go of the tension and feel your body relax.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 이완 운동을 하면 잠이 잘 와요.
examples.en: If I do relaxation exercises before bed, I fall asleep easily.

examples.ko: 스트레스를 받으면 몸의 이완이 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: When I'm stressed, my body doesn't relax well.
In a state of deep relaxation, the mind also becomes calm.
The doctor prescribed a muscle relaxant.

explain: 근육이나 마음의 긴장이 풀리는 것을 말해요. 반대말은 '긴장'이에요. 일상에서는 '긴장을 풀다'라고 많이 하고, '이완'은 운동, 의학, 명상 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 운동이 끝나면 근육 이완 스트레칭을 꼭 해요.
phrases.en: After exercising, I always do relaxation stretches for my muscles.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이완' 앞에 '근육'을 붙인 말로, 운동이나 의학 이야기에서 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This puts 'muscle' before 이완 and is the most common pairing in exercise and medical contexts.

phrases.example: 따뜻한 물에 들어가면 몸이 천천히 이완돼요.
phrases.en: When I get into warm water, my body slowly relaxes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이완'을 동사로 바꾼 말로, 몸이나 근육이 저절로 풀리는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the verb form of 이완 and describes the body or muscles loosening on their own.

phrases.example: 시험 전에는 심호흡을 하면서 긴장을 풀어요.
phrases.en: Before an exam, I relax by taking deep breaths.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이완'과 같은 뜻을 일상 대화에서 말할 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most natural everyday way to express the same idea as 이완.

explain_en: It refers to muscles or the mind letting go of tension. Its opposite is '긴장'. In daily talk people say '긴장을 풀다', while '이완' comes up often in exercise, medicine, and meditation.

examples.ko: 뱀에 물리면 빨리 해독제를 맞아야 해요.
examples.en: If a snake bites you, you must get the antidote quickly.
This hospital has the antidote ready.
The antidote differs depending on the type of poison.

examples.ko: 이 약은 중독 사고에 해독제로 쓰여요.
examples.en: This medicine is used as an antidote in poisoning accidents.
It's even scarier because it's a poison with no antidote.
Developing the antidote took several years.

explain: 독을 풀어 주는 약이에요. 의학 뉴스나 영화에 자주 나오고, 비유로도 많이 써요. 몸속 독을 뺀다는 '해독'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: Laughter is the antidote to stress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 것을 없애 주는 좋은 것을 비유할 때 써요. 글이나 연설에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for something good that counteracts something bad. Common in writing and speeches.

explain_en: This is a medicine that neutralizes poison. It appears often in medical news and movies, and is also commonly used figuratively. It is good to learn it together with '해독' (detoxification).
